limits.description: 1647 Wellcome copy only; no collation of independent original editions or manuscripts.
Source terms CRYSIS, decretory, chrysmal, humour and faculty belong to 1647 usage; not modern clinical constructs.
Galen's alleged sudden-motion definition not collated with Galen's Greek/Latin primary text.
The exception in printed291 belongs to unnamed objectors, not to Hippocrates. The ancient citation remains uncollated.
Avicenna in Canticis reference is Lilly's attribution; underlying source is not examined.
Original volume's p291 l7 'r do' erratum is legible; exact source body token/line convention remains unproved.
Printed295 erratum atram is linked to the relevant body line; damaged original lettering is unresolved.
Illness onset moment has no independent chronological verification in historical example.
Urine first-presentation or first doctor consultation times are fallbacks and expressly less certain.
Lunar longitude, chart houses/aspects and alleged event timings were not calculated against modern independent historical ephemerides.
The printed 16 July 1645 horoscope is reused as an IF/suppose example, not a new chart, patient or outcome.
The 15°42′ Virgo Moon position and 16° Virgo table entry differ by 18 arcminutes due to the author's rounding.
Printed294 table has 64 apparent non-formula numerical readings documented separately in TABLE_PRINT_EXCEPTIONS.json; the model is not a diplomatic transcription.
Printed systematic 60-cell one-degree offset, four isolated non-formula entries, and seven hard-to-read positions require separate source treatment.
Semiquadrate, crisis and indicative labels are printed schematic notions; extension to all phase positions is interpretation.
Moon's motion can vary; no exact clock dates follow from table positions without an independently verified ephemeris.
Conditional benefic judgement specifically says 'if the party be ordained for life'; may make claims unfalsifiable.
Claims about favourable/aspect-based cure and easier medicine are source authorial claims, not trials or treatment guidance.
The 'inferior causes' alternative is acknowledged but neither it nor lunar causation is experimentally assessed.
Humoral, temperamental, purging and sign association claims have no source-supported modern clinical efficacy.
Printed signs in the purging brace/table must not be silently converted into a general therapeutic algorithm.
The cited house-cusp crossings are sixth, seventh, eighth only, not the first.
Aphorisms in previous chapters and the 1645 July illness case are neither rerun nor counted as new independent support here.
Erratum p295 atram matches its original body line but does not authorize a silent body rewrite.
The author does not provide observed patient cohorts, denominators, blind forecast logs or reproducible outcomes.
No source content here validates astronomical astrology, medical diagnostics, or any prospective life prediction.
The following servant-freedom material starts below PDF330 divider and is excluded.
The previous XLVI patient-transit narrative ends above PDF324 divider and is excluded.
Galen/Hippocrates/Avicenna distinctions can influence disease concept but are not independent empirical evidence.
Phrase 'ordained for life' may refer to providential fate, not a measurable frozen criterion.

The earlier question-wheel Moon-like glyph/degree might indicate 15°43′ while Chapter XLVII prose reads 15°42′ Virgo; source pairing and exact minute are not proven. The rounded 16° input is invariant to this one-minute distinction.
The Mars/Sun glyph pair in the historical sign table lacks an explicit either/both operator.
